Checked counters count each value node exactly once; entering each array/object adds container depth; keys share decoded UTF8 string budgets and do not count as value nodes. Object keys enforce entry bounds and duplicate decoded-key membership before reading/inserting the duplicate value. Map/sequence close at the inclusive limit without an extra node.

Decoded strings and keys enforce individual and cumulative byte limits before retained copies. Serde can transiently allocate one escaped token; design explicitly bounds this by original frame and makes no zero-allocation/smaller-than-frame heap claim.
